note: The components the contract defines. The web profile's components.css used to
be written by hand, which meant the styles a consumer shipped and the
contract behind it were two things that could disagree. The stylesheet is
now projected from this file.
A component is stated by the roles it carries, the states it has, the tokens
it uses and the accessibility it owes. The tokens are named, never valued:
the value lives in core/TOKENS.json or core/SURFACES.json, and a component
that names a token the contract does not have is refused.

action.description: The principal contextual operation, with a verb label. A disabled action is still readable, and a focus ring is visible without hover.
note: The text is anthracite, not white. Both pairings are approved and the
white one measures 2.87 against Signal Orange, which is below AA for
body text; the anthracite one measures 6.43. COL-002 asks for white
on Signal Orange, and WCAG exempts the text of an active control from
the contrast requirement, so the rule is a floor and this is above it.

input.description: A field the user types into, with a visible label and a focus treatment that does not depend on hover.

state.description: A state, written in words, with a mark beside it. The mark is a disc and not a capsule: the reference scene shows a status capsule struck out, and CMP-001 forbids it.

a11y.text-carrying: The state is in the words, so the mark is never the only cue.

note: The state is written in words, and the words are the cue; the mark
beside them is a disc, not a capsule, because the reference scene shows a
status capsule struck out and CMP-001 forbids it.
Two states, not three: pending and observed, which is what the state
projection in profiles/web/state.ts declares. A request does not become
an observed success because it was sent - STA-001 - so the pending state
says so in words.

system.description: Technical and metadata text: identifiers, measurements and evidence, set in tabular figures so columns of numbers align.
